From 19fc99d0c6ba7d9b65456496b5bb2169d5f74cd0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2015 18:31:56 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
index e1268f905026..f412b53ed268 100644
--- a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
+++ b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
@@ -449,10 +449,21 @@ static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c`**
- The function `emit_udiv()` has been modified to change the order of loading registers for the division operation.
- A comment block has been added to explain the changes made for handling specific BPF instructions (`BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K` and `BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X`).
- The code now first loads the `rn` register into `ARM_R1` before loading the `rm` register into `ARM_R0`. This prevents the accidental overwriting of `ARM_R0` when `rn` is `ARM_R0` (which is the case for `BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K`).

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The changes in the `emit_udiv()` function are directly related to fixing a bug where the same value could be used for both the dividend and divisor due to the order of register loading. By ensuring that `rn` is loaded into `ARM_R1` first, the patch prevents this issue, thereby improving the correctness of the division operation in the BPF JIT compilation process. The added comments provide clarity on the rationale behind the changes, indicating that the modifications are specifically aimed at addressing potential register overlap issues in certain BPF instruction scenarios.

Here is the commit message:
ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `emit_udiv()` function was called with `rn` set to `ARM_R0` (which is used as a scratch register) and `rm` set to another register. When `rm` was loaded into `ARM_R0` before `rn`, it resulted in both the dividend and divisor being the same, leading to incorrect division operations. This was particularly problematic for BPF instructions that required the use of `ARM_R0` as a source register.

Here is the patch:
 
 static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 {
 #if __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ == 7
 	if (elf_hwcap & HWCAP_IDIVA) {
 		emit(ARM_UDIV(rd, rm, rn), ctx);
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
 	emit_blx_r(ARM_R3, ctx);
 
 	if (rd != ARM_R0)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(rd, ARM_R0), ctx);
 }
